thread:
maria: Quick sync — I'm putting together a synthetic + long-context benchmark to exercise KV cache eviction/paging across realistic interleaved traffic. Goal: catch regressions where reuse windows slip and fragmentation steadily grows over a long session. Planning to add it as a nightly regression job if folks sign off.

raj: SGTM. Can you sketch the workload mix? main risk is the 3x smaller requests repeatedly evicting hot fragments when the long tails arrive.

maria: Draft mix: 70% short prompts (seq_len 128, kv_chunks ~3), 25% medium (512), 5% long (4096+). Interleave pattern with locality windows so hot keys show reuse for ~30-60s. Seeded randomness so runs are reproducible. Command I used: 
```
perf-run --suite=kvcache-evict-synth --seed=2026 --mix short:0.7,med:0.25,long:0.05 --locality=window:45s --ttl-buckets=256,512,1024
```

kevin: Nice. A couple notes from profiling yesterday: when sequence lengths jump from 512->4096 we see a stepwise increase in real memory due to fragmentation in the slab allocator. I attached a tiny flame snippet: 
```
# from heap-prof --alloc-traces
fragmentation_hot: 34%
kv_slot_alloc: 48%
free_coalesce_misses: 17%
```
If the eviction policy leaves small islands of KV slots, reuse goes down even if total free bytes are adequate.

elaine: We should add a deterministic fragmentation reporter to the harness (map of free-span lengths over time) so CI can assert no steady upward trend after 1h synthetic run. I hit a flaky reg where mem growth plateaued for 20m then crept up again. Also: add a failure mode where we throttle batching to expose eviction pressure.

maria: Good call. I'll add two checks: 1) fragmentation_h95 < 40% after 60m, 2) reuse_rate (hot_key hits / hot_key accesses) > 0.9 for the last 15m. Also add batch throttle knob.

raj: For eviction policy, are we testing LRU + localized MRU (keep last N windows pinned)? Might help for repeated short prefixes.

maria: Current impls: LRU segmented + eviction-of-largest-fragment-first (to reduce small-fragment islands). We'll include an alternate run using MRU-protect for hot windows.

perf-bot: nightly-run queued: kvcache-evict-synth @1805126000 (expected ~72m) — will post artifacts to GCS on completion.

kevin: When you add the fragmentation map, include a microtrace correlating request ids -> evicted slot ids. That lets us repro sequences that triggered bad evictions. A tiny log line per eviction is enough: 
```
evict: session=0x5e3 id=1234 slot=0x7f seq_len=4096 reason=fragment_split
```

elaine: Also add a synthetic that intentionally creates many small allocations (to mimic tokenization variance) — fragmentation differences there are more revealing than uniform chunk sizes.

maria: Will do: small-allocation stress case + long interleaved run + batch-throttle stress. Plan to commit to a feature branch today and open a PR with the harness and fail conditions. If CI flaps, we can limit to nightly only.

raj: Sounds good. One ask: annotate the PR with a reproducible minimal repro (seed + timestamp + short log snippet) so if we see a regression we can re-run exact sequence.

maria: Yep. I'll include `--seed` and upload the event stream gz to GCS. Thanks — I'll @everyone when PR is up. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: PR check queued: kvcache/evict-synth - running unit + integration smoke (approx 20m).

kevin: TLDR — this should catch the slow-memory-creep regressions we saw in last week's long-run. If we still see creep, next step is to enable slab coalescing heuristics and re-run.

maria: Agreed. I'll iterate and post a test summary once the nightly finishes.

elaine: Thanks — excited to have a reproducible nightly for this. :rocket:
